name: Norfolk International Airport
before:
The airport for Hampton Roads in south east Virginia, seven miles north east of downtown Norfolk, and it also draws from north east North Carolina. It carried 2,444,897 passengers in 2024, third in Virginia behind Dulles and Reagan National.

It is a compact site of 1,300 acres, with a main runway of 9,001 feet and a shorter crosswind runway. There are two passenger concourses, with American, Southwest and Breeze Airways using Concourse A.

Air traffic control here is busier than the passenger figure suggests. The Norfolk tower, built in 1995 and standing 134 feet high, handles around 1,100 aircraft a day, round the clock, every day of the year.

General aviation is looked after by Signature Flight Support, with a 54,000 square foot facility covering everything from aircraft hire and sightseeing flights to maintenance.
after:
The main airport for Hampton Roads in Virginia, seven miles north east of downtown Norfolk, and it also serves the Outer Banks of North Carolina. It handled almost 4.9 million passengers in 2025, fourth in Virginia behind Dulles, Reagan National and, narrowly, Richmond.

The site covers 1,300 acres, with a single runway of 9,001 feet since the shorter crosswind runway closed in August 2025. There are two passenger concourses, with American and Southwest using Concourse A.

General aviation is looked after by Signature Aviation.

claims.why: Breeze's concourse cannot be confirmed as current. The airport's August 2025 terminal map lists American and Southwest under Concourse A and Breeze among the other airlines; the airport said on 17 April 2026 that Breeze 'will relocate into Concourse A later this spring'; the live board read on 23 September 2026 shows no gate for either Breeze flight. claims.claim: Breeze Airways flies seasonally to Cancún
claims.why: Held back: verified, but a new fact that replaces nothing in the old text. Breeze started seasonal Saturday flights to Cancún on 10 January 2026 (WTKR), the airport lists them as seasonal, one to two a week, and its home page says they resume in December. Worth adding: it is the airport's only international route. The airport's own FAQ still says its airlines fly no nonstop international routes, which is out of date. WAVY and WYDaily reports on the route answered with bot checks and were not tried again.

sources.quote: Starting Jan. 10, 2026, Breeze Airways will have direct flights from Norfolk International Airport to Cancun, Mexico seasonally on Saturdays.
Breeze Airways has flights to Cancun seasonally one to two times a week.

claims.claim: TransformORF works: new international arrivals facility, gates A10 to A12, two security checkpoints for now
claims.why: Held back: new facts that replace nothing, and they rest mostly on the airport's own release of 17 April 2026 (Wikipedia describes the same works as planned). Customs has processed international arrivals in an upgraded facility since March 2026; three gates (A10 to A12) opened on Concourse A in April 2026; screening happens at two separate checkpoints until a single one opens, so a traveller must use the checkpoint for the right concourse. Andy may want the checkpoint point in the text once a second source confirms it.
